With the classic JSX transform, `<div />` compiles to `React.createElement("div")`. The file needs `React` in scope, but the name appears nowhere in the code, so `no-unused-vars` reports the import.

This rule reports nothing itself. While it is on, every JSX element counts as a use of `React`, and `no-unused-vars` leaves the import alone.

If a `@jsx` comment or `settings.react.pragma` names another function, that variable is counted in place of `React`. A `<>` fragment also counts as a use of `Fragment`, or of the name in `settings.react.fragment`.

{/* never reports */}

## Examples

With this rule on, `no-unused-vars` does not report `React` here:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import React from "react";

export function Greeting() {
  return <p>Hello</p>;
}
```

Nor `h` here:

{/* good */}
```jsx
/** @jsx h */
import { h } from "preact";

export function Greeting() {
  return <p>Hello</p>;
}
```

## When not to use it

With the automatic JSX runtime of React 17 and later, you do not import `React` for JSX. Turn this rule off, so that a leftover import is reported.
